why: Deletions a reviewer has judged superseded, keyed by the deleted path.
`node local/sync/post-sync.mjs` inventories the exported surface of every deleted fork-only module
and fails when an export has no surviving reference. That is the right default: a module disappearing
is exactly when a caller can leave with it. This file is how a reviewed supersession is recorded so
the check can pass without weakening it.
Each entry must name the live replacement and the evidence for calling it a superset — the check
prints this, so the next sync inherits the reasoning instead of re-deriving it.
An entry whose path is no longer deleted is reported as stale, so this file cannot rot unnoticed.

src/main/ipc/filesystem/filesystem-quick.reason: The fork's listing behaviour survived the handoff: `fs:listFiles` still accepts `nameFilter` and matches its whitespace-separated tokens (args at line 40, matching at 98-110), and `fs:cancelListFiles` is still registered. The module's channel was not dropped, only re-homed.

src/relay/quick-open-list-line-processor.reason: Compared branch by branch: root-relative normalisation, the unparseable-record return, the blocklist backstop, exclude prefixes, the name-filter dotfile scope, matcher delivery, dedupe, maxResults truncation, the counted-line return, and the decode/cancel/symlink/separator framing all have live counterparts. It was a pure module, so the deletion lost no behaviour of its own. The behaviour that WAS lost sat in the other deleted module and has been restored rather than acknowledged away: the worker-owned index warm at fs:listFiles and cancelLocalConsumer(senderId) at fs:cancelListFiles had no caller left while fs:searchFilePaths still submitted index queries under that consumer id, so a cancelled filter left its worker query running. Both are restored in filesystem-search-handlers.ts and pinned by filesystem-quick-open-path-index-wiring.test.ts.

src/main/ipc/filesystem/filesystem-text-.reason: Upstream's handler registers the same `fs:search` channel and adds `fs:cancelSearch` with sender-scoped cancellation, which the fork's extracted handler never had. A superset, verified by reading both registrations.
